name: mcp-stashbox
description: MCP server for the public stash-box metadata catalogues. Search scenes, performers, studios and tags across the public stash-box catalogues.
long_description:
Reads the public stash-box catalogues for scenes, performers, studios and tags. These catalogues hold metadata and no media: a record names where something was published and carries nothing of it.

The server asks every catalogue you have configured and keeps the seams visible. A catalogue that failed, one that was never asked and one that looked and found nothing are three different things, and every answer says which is which. Counts are never added across catalogues and rows are never ranked against each other, because they publish no score in common.

The fingerprint route is the reason to ask several at once. MD5 and OSHASH match the same file byte for byte; PHASH matches images that resemble each other, which covers a re-encode, a crop and a different scene from one shoot. Every match says which kind of claim it is, and a catalogue that counts no disputes over a fingerprint reports an unknown contest.

tools.name: get_sources
tools.description: Say what each configured catalogue answers, and where no key is held.

tools.name: search_scenes
tools.description: Search scenes across every configured catalogue.

query.description: Words for the catalogue's own text index, which reads them as a union. It is exclusive with the typed arguments, which narrow as an intersection.

alias.description: No catalogue's faceted route applies it, though every faceted input declares it: a request carrying it answers as wide as one carrying none, so it is never sent and the answer names it as a narrowing nobody received.

date_compare.description: These catalogues compare a date against one bound and answer no range, so the comparison is written rather than assumed.

match.description: How performer_ids and tag_ids are read, which are the only arguments it governs. 'all', the default, asks for scenes carrying every identifier of a list; 'any' for scenes carrying at least one, which answers counts an order of magnitude wider. A scene names one studio, so studio_ids asks for any of its identifiers under both readings. The lists narrow against each other as an intersection either way.

page.description: Which page of its own order every catalogue asked is read at, counted from 1. A search written with words alone reads the first rows each text index answers with, since those routes take no page.

limit.description: How many rows one page of one catalogue carries. An answer holding several carries up to this many from each: their pages are their own and nothing here interleaves them into one.

tools.name: get_scene
tools.description: Read one scene, from the catalogue its identifier names.

sections.description: The blocks read beside the record's own fields, which come back whatever is written here. Each name adds a block, and 'basic' asks for those fields alone.

prefer.description: The order the catalogues are preferred in where they disagree on a field. Left out, the registry's own order stands, and every card states the order applied.
